{{Quote|Viceroy, we have captured the Queen."<br />"Ah, victory.|OOM-9 and Viceroy Nute Gunray|audio=AhVictory-TPM.flac|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
The '''Capture of Theed'''&mdash;also known as the '''Fall of Theed''', the '''Invasion of Theed''', or, in regards to [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala's]] escape, the '''Escape from Naboo'''&mdash;was a battle during the opening stages of the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. After a series of quick victories, the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[OOM command battle droid/Legends|OOM command battle droid]] [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]] attacked the [[City/Legends|city]] with a force of battle droids and [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tanks]] and [[Energy pummel/Legends|Heavy Energy Pummels]]. He went through the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]]' [[Fortress/Legends|defenses]] and fended off attacks from [[V-19 landspeeder|Gian speeders]] to destroy a [[Theed signal jammer|signal jammer]]. Once in front of the [[Theed Royal Palace/Legends|Theed Royal Palace]], he used [[OX9]] [[Labor droid/Legends|labor droids]] protected by [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|droid starfighters]] to construct a [[Neimoidian Throne]] as a symbol of the Federation's victory. [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], leader of the Trade Federation, landed soon after. [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] Amidala, her head of security [[Quarsh Panaka/Legends|Quarsh Panaka]], several [[Handmaiden/Legends|handmaidens]], and Theed's [[Governor/Legends|governor]] [[Sio Bibble/Legends|Sio Bibble]] were all captured. Gunray tried to force Queen Amidala to sign a treaty legitimizing the invasion, and when she refused Gunray ordered her and her entourage to be sent to [[Camp Four/Legends|Camp Four]].

The [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] negotiators [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], who had been the victims of a [[Mission to Naboo|failed assassination]] at the hands of the Trade Federation onboard the [[Saak'ak/Legends|blockade flagship]], arrived in Theed along with the native [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]]. Jinn ordered Kenobi to reach the Palace. The younger Jedi went through the streers, engaging battle droids and rescuing hostages. He then met several Naboo guards who informed him of a secret entrance to the Palace, which Kenobi entered after destroying a [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|Single Trooper Aerial Platform]]. They were separated from each other when an Armored Assault Tank blew up a [[bridge]] they were trying to cross. Kenobi swam away and got back on the streets and proceeded through the garden. He was able to gain entrance to the gates of the Palace. During the battle, the two Jedi went through the city and rescued several handmaidens from [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]] and [[P-series droideka/Legends|destroyer droids]]. They also commandeered a [[Tank/Legends|tank]]. Near the Palace they fought [[Flame battle droid]]s and a [[T4 turret droid]].

Once inside the Royal Palace, Kenobi escorted the servant [[Asha (Naboo)|Asha]] through the Palace to the throne room. They were too late to rescue the Queen, and he had to duel three [[Trade Federation assassin droid]]s. A guard informed them the Queen had been taken to Camp Four, and Kenobi left to look for her. The two Jedi also fought through the Palace, engaging battle droids and [[B1 grapple droid/Legends|B1 grapple droids]], and went to the throne room via a secret entrance. Once outside the Palace, Kenobi updated Jinn, who told him to regroup. Kenobi helped the Naboo guards destroy an Armored Assault Tank with [[Ion grenade/Legends|ion grenades]] before continuing. He joined back up with Jinn and Binks, and the two rescued the Queen and her entourage from [[OOM-series security droid/Legends|OOM security battle droids]].

Jinn convinced the Queen to go to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to plead her case before the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. The group went to the [[Theed Hangar/Legends|Theed Hangar]] and liberated the [[J-type 327 Nubian royal starship/Legends|Royal Starship]] which they used to escape the [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] blockade. Damage to the [[Hyperdrive motivator/Legends|hyperdrive motivator]] forced them to take refuge on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Before they left, Panaka ordered an evacuation of the city. Captain Kael and [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Gavyn Sykes/Legends|Gavyn Sykes]] fled the city after stealing [[STAP-2]]s, while other officers, including [[Palmer (Royal Naboo Security Forces)|Palmer]], were captured.

==Prelude==
===The Invasion of Naboo===
{{Quote|This turn of events is unfortunate. We must accelerate our plans. Begin landing your troops.|Darth Sidious to Nute Gunray|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
[[File:Trade_Federation_Invasion.png|thumb|right|300px|The Trade Federation's C-9979 landing crafts approach Naboo]]
In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], as part of the [[Grand Plan/Legends|Grand Plan]] to bring [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] under [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] dominion, the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], who was known publicly as [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] Palpatine of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], orchestrated the passage<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> of [[Senate Resolution BR-0371]], which enforced the taxation of the [[Free Trade Zone/Legends|Free Trade Zones]] in the Mid and [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rims]].<ref name="The Essential Chronology">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref> The resolution significantly impacted the profits of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation of Planets]], whose [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Viceroy]], [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], was persuaded to lead an [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in protest of BR-0371 by Sidious to further the Sith Lord's purposes. The invasion began with a [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] of Naboo<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> six [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the passage of the resolution.<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds" />

The blockade involved a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of [[Lucrehulk-class LH-3210 cargo freighter/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class LH-3210 cargo freighters]] surrounding the planet and halting all commerce.<ref name="Complete Cross-Sections">''[[Star Wars: Complete Cross-Sections]]''</ref> A month after the blockade began, the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] [[Mission to Naboo|dispatched]] two [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassadors]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], to negotiate with the Trade Federation to resolve the crisis. Gunray was frightened by their appearance and contacted Sidious, who ordered him to [[Death/Legends|kill]] the Jedi and begin the invasion earlier than scheduled by landing the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Army]] on Naboo. The Jedi were able to escape and stowed aboard [[Unidentified C-9979 landing craft|separate]] [[C-9979 landing craft/Legends|C-9979 landing crafts]].<ref name="Episode I" />

===March towards Theed===
{{Quote|A communications disruption can mean only one thing—invasion.|Sio Bibble|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
[[File:Communications_disruption.png|thumb|left|300px|Naboo's communications with the wider galaxy were severed while the Queen's council had a holographic meeting with Senator Palpatine.]]
Sidious gave the [[Droid/Legends|Droid]] [[Army/Legends|Army]] two objectives for the invasion: to sever Naboo's communications and to force the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]] to sign a treaty of surrender. The crafts mostly landed in remote locations to avoid detection by Naboo's populace. An elite group landed in the planet's northern hemisphere, where the Human [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of Theed was located. The Naboo radar arrays detected the Federation invasion force but the [[Naboo Royal Space Fighter Corps/Legends|Naboo Royal Space Fighter Corps]] radar operators were shocked at the scale of the force. The pilots waited for the order to strike, but Queen Amidala remained convinced of a peaceful solution to the situation and did not order a response.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" />

Meanwhile, [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|droid starfighters]] attacked airborne [[Transport/Legends|transports]] in order to force them into landing. One vessel, the passenger freighter [[Crescent (freighter)|''Crescent'']] captained by [[Nuun Pargen]], was fired upon and forced to set down on the edge of the [[Great Grass Plains/Legends|Great Grass Plains]] outside of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]], Naboo's capital city. Pargen's daughter, [[Inea Pargen|Inea]], was injured in the attack. Captain Pargen asked the students to return to Theed to retrieve the medical supplies necessary to stabilize Inea while he repaired the ship.<ref name="PoN">{{WizCite|book=Secrets of Naboo|story=Peril on Naboo}}</ref> 

[[File:Trade_Federation_Droid_Army.png|thumb|right|300px|The Droid Army marches towards Theed]]
The [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droid]] [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]] led one of the first attacks, [[Subjugation of Parrlay|destroying]] [[Transmitter/Legends|transmitters]] at the cities of [[Vis/Legends|Vis]], [[New Centrif]], and [[Parrlay]] to prevent the Naboo from communicating with the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]].<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds" /> This disruption interupted a holographic meeting between Palpatine on Coruscant and Amidala and the [[Naboo Royal Advisory Council/Legends|Naboo Royal Advisory Council]] in Theed, announcing to them that the invasion had begun.<ref name="Episode I" /> OOM-9 [[Capture of Harte Secur|moved on]] to [[Invasion of Spinnaker|capture]] the cities of [[Harte Secur]] and [[Spinnaker/Legends|Spinnaker]], the latter of which was a short distance from Theed.<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds" /> The Droid Army took strategic positions on the planet [[Standard day/Legends|overnight]], ready to strike at Theed on the morning after their landing.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> Meanwhile, Jinn and Kenobi reunited in the [[Gungan Swamp]]s and encountered one of the indigenous [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]]: [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]]. He led them to the [[Water/Legends|underwater]] Gungan capital [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], from which the Jedi acquired a [[Tribubble bongo/Legends|tribubble bongo]] which, with Binks's help, they used to navigate the waterways through Naboo's planetary core to reach Theed. Their journey was impeded by encounters with large creatures native to Naboo, including an [[Opee sea killer/Legends|opee sea killer]], a [[Colo claw fish/Legends|colo claw fish]], and a [[Sando aqua monster/Legends|sando aqua monster]].<ref name="Episode I" />

The droids that marched towards Theed were held in thirty-three large transports, which each contained 112 [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]], 342 [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tanks]], and other infantry and [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]]. Each vehicle and [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droid]] were programmed with a map of the city and given key objectives to execute.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> Multiple bridges within the city were destroyed in order to slow down the Trade Federation's progress.<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds" /> The battle droids also had orders to capture or kill any Royal Naboo Security Forces personnel they encountered.<ref name="Fact File 29">{{FactFile|29|NAB 11-16|The Capture of Theed}}</ref> As the passengers of the ''Crescent'' reached Theed, the city was in a state of chaos as the residents of the outer sectors had spotted the approaching Droid Army. The passengers therefore attempted to find the medical supplies for Inea Pargen swiftly.<ref name="PoN" />

==The capture==
===Fighting in Theed===
====Capture of the city====
{{Quote|OOM-9, the time has come to take the city of Theed. Target only offensive units|Nute Gunray, to OOM-9|audio=Theed-GunraysOrders.flac|<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds" />}}
[[File:OOM-9_Fall_of_Theed.png|thumb|left|300px|OOM-9 and a portion of the Droid Army at the gates of Theed]]
The Trade Federation Droid Army struck in the morning, catching the citizens of Theed unaware.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> Some panicked citizens tried to flee but were unable to escape.<ref name="Fact File 29" /> As the army approached Theed, Gunray made a transmission to Sidious, informing him of their imminent victory. The Droid Army had occupied the surrounding countryside and Queen Amidala had advised her military to stand down, although the Trade Federation expected sporadic resistance throughout the city. A [[Theed signal jammer|signal jammer]] near the [[Theed Hangar/Legends|Theed Hangar]] complex prevented the Federation from sending in transports and droid starfighters. OOM-9, in a [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Heavy Armored Assault Tank]], personally led a battalion of elite units into Theed. His forces consisted of eight AATs, two [[Energy pummel/Legends|Heavy Energy Pummels]], three [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|Single Trooper Aerial Platforms]], and sixteen [[Heavy Battle Droid/Legends|Heavy battle droids]].<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds" />

They broke through the southern gates of Theed and advanced northeast toward the signal jammer,<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds" /> using the pummels<ref name="GB Prima">[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref> to destroy two [[Fortress/Legends|fortresses]] and other military buildings they encountered on the path.<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds" /> The droids sent their [[Tank/Legends|tanks]] in first ahead of the infantry, crushing through fountains and arbors.<ref name="Warfare cut">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-6-showdown-at-naboo|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 6: Showdown at Naboo}}</ref> The Trade Federation's strategy also involved spreading their forces out through the city while working towards Theed Palace.<ref name="Fact File 29" /> The [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] sent [[V-19 landspeeder|Gian speeders]] and infantry forces against the Droid Army to no avail. The droid forces destroyed the signal jammer, and OOM-9 reported its destruction to Gunray. The Viceroy sent more reinforcements to the western side of Theed. These consisted of four [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]], four AATs, two energy pummels, two [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|Single Strooper Aerial Platforms (STAP)]], and six [[OX9]] [[Labor droid/Legends|labor droids]]. Gunray ordered OOM-9 to get at least five battle [[Droid/Legends|droids]] within the grounds of the Royal Palace, after which they would use the OX9s to build a [[Neimoidian Throne]] next to the Palace to symbolize their control of the city.<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds" />

The two Trade Federation groups linked up and proceeded up the [[Main Boulevard]] to the [[Theed Royal Palace/Legends|Theed Royal Palace]]. The droid forces destroyed the gates blocking their path along with two additional Fortresses. When the droids occupied the palace grounds, more labor droids, along with five droid starfighters, arrived. The labor droids were ordered to construct a [[Neimoidian Throne]]. After it was completed, a pleased Gunray congratulated OOM-9 for capturing Theed before telling him to capture the queen.<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds" /> Once the majority of the city was under Trade Federation control, the battle droids adopted a slightly less aggressive stance designed to prevent the queen from escaping. This made it easier for determined individuals to hide or escape Theed, as long as they did not attack the battle droids or otherwise resist.<ref name="Fact File 29" /> 

[[File:Padme_watches.png|thumb|right|300px|Queen Amidala mournfully watches the Fall of Theed.]]
Queen Amidala watched the invasion from a window in the Royal Palace while looking down in sadness<ref name="Episode I" /> and witnessed the shooting of a woman who had defied a battle droid's orders. Amidala then called in her [[Handmaiden/Legends|handmaiden]] [[Sabé/Legends|Sabé]] to enact a security plan<ref name="Episode I Journal">''[[Star Wars Journal: Queen Amidala]]''</ref> ordered by Panaka<ref name="Fact File 29" /> in which Sabé presented herself as Queen Amidala while Padmé herself assumed the role of a handmaiden. Sabé wore the queen's [[Black traveling gown/Legends|black traveling gown]], and Padmé also gave Sabé an [[Padmé Amidala's amulet|amulet]] given to her by her [[Parent/Legends|parents]], vowing to herself that she would not wear it again until Naboo was free. As battle droids waited for her in a hallway, Amidala recorded the events of the day in her [[Padmé Amidala's journal|journal]], unsure of when she would have time for another entry.<ref name="Episode I Journal" />

====Escapees====
{{Quote|This is Captain Panaka. I am ordering all officers to clear the city at once. Do not engage the enemy except in self-defense. We don't want a war in our streets.|Captain Quarsh Panaka's evacuation order to the officers of the Royal Naboo Security Forces|<ref name="Star Wars: Battle for Naboo" />}}
[[File:Theedriot.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Fights in the streets of Theed.]]
While Amidala adopted her disguise, Panaka ordered all Royal Naboo Security Forces personnel to abandon their duties and escape to the forests and swamps, where they could regroup and organize an organized [[Naboo Resistance|resistance]].<ref name="Fact File 29" /> He also called for the use of violence only in self-defence to avoid a war in the streets of Theed.<ref name="Star Wars: Battle for Naboo" /> The first [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] of the invasion had been filled with chaotic street battles. The Naboo [[Teckla Minnau/Legends|Teckla Minnau]] and her half-sister [[Nandi]] fled to the planet's [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]] along with elements of the Royal Naboo Security Forces in that time.<ref name="Teckla Databank">{{DB|character|teckla|Minnau, Teckla}}</ref> The passengers of the ''Crescent'' escaped Theed by taking a [[Speeder/Legends|speeder]] across the Solleu River, encountering an MTT and a STAP patrol on their way until they reached safety. A group of students from Theed's [[Royal House of Learning/Legends|Royal House of Learning]], including the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Rorworr (Naboo)|Rorworr]] and the Gungan [[Toba]], also escaped undetected.<ref name="Fact File 29" /> The passengers of the ''Crescent'' had gathered medical supplies for Inea and attempted to return to the ship during the battle, and had difficulty doing so. As they fought their way out, they attempted to aid the resisting Naboo where they could, which included helping overwhelmed Royal Naboo Security Forces soldiers defeat an overwhelming battle droid attack. The group were informed of the plan to create a resistance movement.<ref name="Fact File 29" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo}}
The members of [[Bravo Squadron/Legends|Bravo Flight]] heeded Panaka's evacuation order and fled the city. [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Gavyn Sykes/Legends|Gavyn Sykes]] fought his way through a number of droid forces, rescuing a number of captured civilians in the process, before receiving a transmission from [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Kael (officer)|Kael]], who was pinned down near the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces headquarters]]. Sykes destroyed the destroyer droids attacking Kael. Together, they destroyed or went around other battle droids and Armored Assault Tanks. Kael ordered Sykes to follow him as they moved through the plaza to escape into the swamps. Along the way, Sykes picked up a vehicular upgrade. They then arrived at a hangar<ref name="Star Wars: Battle for Naboo" /> in a square on the outskirts of Theed<ref name="Fact File 29" /> protected by two tanks. Kael ordered Sykes to destroy them, and the captain realized the tanks were protecting [[STAP-2]]s. The two stole the speeders and escaped into the countryside.<ref name="Star Wars: Battle for Naboo" />
{{Endgame}}

====Occupation and Jedi arrival====
{{Quote|They drove tanks in ahead of the droids, big ugly things that smashed through the fountains and the arbors and anything else in their way. I remember in Theed the piazzas were full of water and purple musk-rose petals from everything they’d broken. And then came the clankers, the B1 battle droids. They looked weak, with their limbs like saplings, and they were slow and dumb. But that wasn’t the point. There were so many of them, and the Trade Federation had eyes in the sky. We were blind, outgunned, outnumbered. If you fought, you died.|Pars Varqom's recollection of the Fall of Theed, recorded in the Royal Archives of Naboo|<ref name="Warfare cut" />}}
[[File:Theed_Plaza.png|thumb|right|350px|The droids occupy the Palace Plaza.]]
The entire city had fallen shortly after [[Naboo (star)/Legends|sunrise]], too quickly for any substantial defense to be arranged. Any available [[Weapon/Legends|weapons]] had been confiscated and battle droids patrolled Theed for any remaining resistance. The Trade Federation began relocating the Naboo to newly constructed detention camps outside the city.<ref name="TPM novel" /> Inside Theed Hangar, the Naboo [[air traffic controller]]s were captured.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> [[Naboo Palace Guard/Legends|Palace Guard]] [[Pars Varqom]] saw Theed's piazza's full of water and musk-rose petals carelessly broken by the droids. According to Varqom, anyone who fought against the battle droids were killed by their overwhelming numbers and air supremacy.<ref name="Warfare cut" /> Due to the swiftness of the invasion, many of the buildings in Theed remained intact, although the [[Palace Courtyard/Legends|Palace Courtyard]] was severely bombed by Armored Assault Tanks.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" />

After the city was under Trade Federation control, the Jedi's bongo breached the surface of the [[Solleu River/Legends|Solleu River]] inside the city limits.<ref name="Episode I" /> As it did, the bongo was pulled along by the currents to a waterfall. Jinn ordered Kenobi to restart the bongo, but its engines failed. The Jedi Master then launched a [[Grappling hook/Legends|grappling hook]] into the canal walls, which prevented the bongo from descending down the waterfall. The two Jedi pulled themselves along the hook line to reach safety while Binks panicked in the bongo. The Gungan left the vessel just in time.<ref name="Complete Saga">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''</ref> As the Jedi pulled Binks out of the canal, a B1 battle droid,<ref name="Episode I: Obi-Wan Kenobi">''[[Episode I: Obi-Wan Kenobi]]''</ref> [[3B3]],<ref name="Insider's Guide">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref> approached them and ordered them to halt. Jinn cut the droid down just as it fired a shot from its blaster, hitting the cable and sending the bongo over the waterfall.<ref name="Episode I: Obi-Wan Kenobi" /> With the droid destroyed, the Jedi looked towards Theed Palace and proceeded to it.<ref name="Mighty Chronicles">[[The Phantom Menace (Mighty Chronicles)|''The Phantom Menace'' Mighty Chronicles adaptation]]</ref>

===Capture of the queen===
{{Quote|The queen and I will sign a treaty that will legitimize our occupation here. I have assurances it will be ratified by the Senate.''"<br />"''I will not cooperate.''"<br />"''Now, now, your highness. In time the suffering of your people will persuade you to see our point of view.|Nute Gunray and Sabé, the latter disguised as Queen Amidala|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
[[File:GunrayAmidalaBibbleTheedRoyalPalace-TPM.png|thumb|left|350px|Nute Gunray descends the stairs of Theed Royal Palace with the captive Queen Amidala.]]
After the fighting in the city had ended,<ref name="Fact File 29" /> Amidala and Sabé were captured by the Trade Federation along with [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka/Legends|Quarsh Panaka]], head of the Royal Naboo Security Forces, [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Sio Bibble/Legends|Sio Bibble]], several Palace Guards, and the handmaidens; [[Rabé/Legends|Rabé]], [[Eirtaé/Legends|Eirtaé]], [[Saché/Legends|Saché]], and [[Yané/Legends|Yané]].<ref name="Expanded" /> The sight of battle droids in Theed Palace made Amidala want to weep, but she was determined not to give the invaders the satisfaction of seeing her in tears.<ref name="TPM junior">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (junior novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' junior novelization]]</ref> With the city under their control, Nute Gunray and Rune Haako travelled down to the planet, a rare move for them as they normally remained in their battleships. Both Neimoidians, however, were eager to visit Theed Palace and see its treasures.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> The Neimoidians landed in their personal [[Sheathipede-class transport shuttle/Legends|''Sheathipede''-class transport shuttle]], OOM-9 then reported the success of the queen's capture to the viceroy, causing Gunray to declare with pride that it was a victory.<ref name="Episode I" />

Gunray and Haako met with the queen and her entourage in the Royal Palace's [[Throne room (Theed Royal Palace)/Legends|throne room]], with a dozen battle droids holding the Naboo hostage. Bibble chastised the Neimoidians for intefering with Naboo's communications, but Gunray was disinterested in his protests.<ref name="TPM novel" /> As the droids escorted the queen and her group down the stairs of Theed Palace, Gunray revealed his plan for the queen to sign a treaty of surrender.<ref name="Episode I" /> Sabé, as Padmé had coached her, rejected Gunray,<ref name="Episode I Journal" /> who ordered the droids to take the queen and her entourage to [[Camp Four/Legends|Camp Four]].<ref name="Episode I" /> The B1 battle droid [[3B3-21/Legends|3B3-21]] was assigned to escort the queen,<ref name="3B2-21">{{CCG|set=Theed Palace Limited|cardname=3B3-21}}</ref> and ten [[OOM-series security droid/Legends|OOM security battle droids]] fulfilled the order.<ref name="Mighty Chronicles" /> Amidala was in awe as she walked through the [[Palace Plaza/Legends|Palace Plaza]], which was normally filled with the sounds of street vendors and [[Musician/Legends|musicians]], and was then full of Trade Federation tanks and droids.<ref name="Episode I Journal" />

===Jedi infiltration===
====Finding the way====
{{Quote|If you're going into the city alone, you're the one that needs help.|A wounded Naboo guard to Kenobi|<ref name="E1 vg" />}}
{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)}}
Jinn told his Padawan that he would create a diversion while Kenobi found a way into the Palace, and cautioned his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] to avoid entanglements. Kenobi went up the stairs near the bongo and engaged several B1-Series battle droids. That way did not lead to the Palace, so he returned to the Solleu and swam to the other side. He then climbed onto the streets and dispatched the two battle droids in his way, and started toward the Palace. He fought through the battle droids stationed in the streets and rescued three hostages. He also sliced his [[Obi-Wan Kenobi's first lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] through the alarm systems, disabling them. At one point, he climbed up the balcony and picked up a [[Sniper rifle/Legends|sniper rifle]] to reduce the number of enemies in his way. He then moved forward across a bridge over the river. Down the street, a shield blocked one street, so he went through a door and climbed the stairs to the upper balcony. There he found another hostage; he rescued the man, who led the Jedi to a balcony to spy on more prisoners. Kenobi then moved past the nearby statue.<ref name="SW:OW" />

A droid starfighter destroyed the [[bridge]] to the Palace. Stuck on the wrong side, Kenobi met two Naboo soldiers and a [[Grenadier/Legends|grenadier]]. They helped him find another way around and told him about a secret entrance to the Palace. Kenobi went up the stairs to the next level and saved another hostage, who warned him about nearby battle droids. Moving along the cliff to the other side, the young Jedi faced more battle droids and one of the Federation's new [[Trade Federation assassin droid|assassin droids]]. He defeated all the droids. He then took over a [[Moog-3000 Death Synthesizer|gun turret]] to destroy a Single Trooper Aerial Platform. He then jumped across the ledges, went up the stairs, and shut off the water flow to the pool. That revealed the secret stairs for him to go down into.<ref name="SW:OW" />
{{Endgame}}

====Kenobi's path====
During the Jedi's trek through the city, the central bridge across the river was blasted apart by an Armored Assault Tank, cutting the city off from other regions. Kenobi was separated from Jinn and Binks. The Jedi were forced to cross the city to find the Queen.<ref name="E1 vg" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)}}
[[File:Obi-Wan_repeater_cannon.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Kenobi fighting in the city.]]
Kenobi jumped into the river and swam away from the tank. He climbed onboard one of the islands a nearby plaza and went onto the walkway. He then [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force push|Force pushed]] a lever to extend the walkway. Continuing onward, he then fought a group of battle droids. A force field generator blocked his path, but Kenobi used the Force to flick a switch and lowered the dam, shorting out the generator. Walking along the path and turning left, he found himself among a firefight with more droids and two Naboo guards. After a conversation with them, he told them he was going to enter the garden, and the soldier gave the Jedi a [[Light repeating blaster/Legends|light repeating blaster]]. Two [[Multi-Troop Transport/Legends|Multi-Troop Transports]] settled over the garden and disgorged droids. Kenobi met a [[Unidentified wounded Naboo guard 1|wounded guard]], who told Kenobi the passcode to enter the gates near the palace. Kenobi then moved forward, avoiding an Armored Assault Tank in the plaza and sneaking around a battle droids and a disabled Multi-Troop Transport. Kenobi gave the password to another Palace Guard. Once through the gates, the guard charged forward but was gunned down.<ref name="E1 vg" />

Kenobi then moved through the door and into the plaza. He found the button to open the door out of the gardens, then went through it. Off in a small alley rested a droid starfighter, which self-destructed as Kenobi approached. Returning to the path, the Jedi then drained several water pools to reveal the controls to the bridge to access the plaza near the palace. He also destroyed the droids near the controls.<ref name="E1 vg" />

Kenobi crossed the bridge and climbed the stairs at the end of the walkway, which had been [[Mine/Legends|mined]], then neared the palace gates, where another Armored Assault Tank was stationed. The Jedi avoided the laser blasts long enough to Force push the lever to open the inner gates, then went back across the tank's path to throw the switch to open the inner gates, which was hidden behind a window. Kenobi then ran through the gates into the area near the palace.<ref name="E1 vg" />
{{Endgame}}

====Into the Palace====
{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles}}
During the battle, Kenobi rejoined Jinn, and they infiltrated Theed and fought through a city littered with more than 20 battle droids and [[OOM-series security droid/Legends|OOM security battle droids]] to make it to the Royal Palace. They passed the [[Theed Royal Library]], which had been turned into a war room for the Droid Army. Juast past the library, they faced a guantlet of [[Missile launcher/Legends|missile launcher]]-armed droids on the balcony and six [[P-series droideka/Legends|destroyer droids]] on the road. At one point, the Jedi commandeered an Armored Assault Tank after taking out its 3 [[OOM pilot battle droid/Legends|pilot droids]] and used it to travel through Theed, blasting other [[Tank/Legends|tanks]] and droids. They also rescued seven handmaidens who had been captured. They disembarked from the tank near the Palace grounds. As they moved onto the palace grounds, they faced more battle droids. In front of the palace they destroyed a [[T4 turret droid]] along with [[Flame battle droid]]s.<ref name="SWJPB" />
{{Endgame}}

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)}}
After entering the palace through the secret entrance, Kenobi found himself inside the palace kitchen, where he met the servant Asha. She told him the Palace was on lockdown, but she could crack the codes. Kenobi climbed up the fireplace to reach the next level and fought the droids in the dining room. He then hit the switch to raise the dining table up from the kitchen, which Asha rode up. She then [[Slicer/Legends|sliced]] the doors for the Jedi, but held back as Kenobi fought off the battle and destroyer droids in the next room. Once all the droids were destroyed, Asha sliced the next door for him. In the next room, Kenobi was cut off by force fields. He destroyed the droids, including an assassin droid, and then shut down the force field for Asha. The codes had been changed, but she sliced the doors.<ref name="SW:OW" />

Through the next doors, the Jedi entered a firefight with Panaka and other Naboo soldiers. Asha was locked out by force fields. Together, Kenobi and the Naboo soldiers destroyed the attacking battle droids and the destroyer droid. Kenobi then unlocked the force fields, and went into the next room with a double staircase and fought more droids. Asha then unlocked the throne room. The group entered and fought three assassin droids, which burst through the windows. A Palace Guard informed them that the Queen had been taken to [[Camp Four/Legends|Camp Four]] to sign a treaty.<ref name="SW:OW" />
{{Endgame}}

===Escape from Naboo===
====Jedi rescue====
{{Quote|We're ambassadors for the Supreme Chancellor.''"<br />"''Your negotiations seem to have failed.''"<br />"''The negotiations never took place. It's urgent that we make contact with the Republic.|Qui-Gon Jinn and Sio Bibble after the former rescued Queen Amidala|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)}}
Kenobi contacted his Master and informed him of the situation. Jinn ordered Kenobi to meet back up. Traveling back outside of the palace, Kenobi met a a [[Unidentified grenadier|Naboo grenadier]], who informed the Jedi about an Armored Assault Tank blocking the resistance. Kenobi jumped on the balcony and destroyed a [[Grenade droid/Legends|grenade droid]]. He then took over a repeater cannon and destroyed two droids on a lower balcony which were manning more repeater cannons. Moving forward, the young Jedi disabled a force field blocking the street and then assisted several resistance members in fighting battle droids, then dropped an [[Ion grenade/Legends|ion grenade]] on the tank, disabling it. The destruction of the tank cleared his way to the next street. Kenobi then deactivated the shield generator blocking his way, and stepped through.<ref name="SW:OW" />

The two Jedi entered the palace and fought through more droids, including [[B1 grapple droid/Legends|B1 grapple droids]], destroyer droids, and OOM command battle droids. At one point they [[Force jump/Legends|Force jumped]] on the outside of the walls, using the balconies to proceed to the next story. After that, they infiltrated the throne room with the help of one of the handmaidens they had rescued, who showed them a secret entrance.<ref name="SWJPB" /><ref name="Episode I Game">At this point the game diverges from {{Film|I}}.This article assumes the rest of the mission is non-canon.</ref>
{{Endgame}}

[[File:Theed_rescue.png|thumb|left|300px|Jinn and Kenobi rescue the Queen.]]
As the queen's entourage reached an avenue leading to the outskirts of the city,<ref name="TPM novel" /> Jinn, Kenobi, and Binks snuck onto a balcony near the palace<ref name="TPM junior" /> just as the group walked beneath it. Together, the Jedi leapt down and activated their lightsabers. Kenobi kicked two of the battle droids while Jinn began cutting them down. The Jedi Master also used the force to push two of the battle droids against a wall. Jinn suggested that the group leave the streets, and Panaka ordered his Palace Guards to take the droid's [[E-5 blaster rifle/Legends|E-5 blaster rifles]].<ref name="Episode I" /> Jinn explained that he and Kenobi were the Chancellor's ambassadors and that they needed to make contact with the Republic. Panaka responded that Naboo's communications had been disabled, leading Jinn to inquire about any available transports. Panaka led the group towards Theed Hangar<ref name="Episode I" /> through backstreets and alleyways. They moved quietly amidst the growing alarm sounds and buzz of STAPs flying overhead.<ref name="TPM novel" /> Jinn remained calm in an effort to ease the fears of those now under his protection.<ref name="Mighty Chronicles" />

====Kenobi and the queen====
{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)}}
On their way to enter the passage under the Palace, Kenobi and the Queen were separated from Jinn, Panaka and the others. The Queen led Kenobi away from a group of charging battle droids and into a Palace corridor. She informed him about a secret passage through the garden, and they headed that way. In the garden, Kenobi saved the Queen from a battle droid. He then pushed a statue out of the way so they could access the passage. They went up the stairs, with Kenobi dispatching another droid. The door to the passage was locked, so Kenobi Force-jumped across the broken balcony and accessed the door's control from the other side, and the two move out into the streets.<ref name="E1 vg" />

Kenobi went into an apartment and met a [[Unidentified Theed woman 1|woman]] who was distraught after being separated from her son. Kenobi promised to rescue the [[Unidentified boy|son]]. The boy had hid from battle droids in a nearby building and Kenobi brought him back to his mother. The woman gave the Jedi a [[Medkit|health pack]] in return. Kenobi also found a [[Unidentified wounded Naboo guard 2|wounded Naboo guard]] nearby. In return for Kenobi fetching him water, the guard warned him about a nearby Armored Assault Tank. Kenobi then snuck around the balcony to flank the tank, and destroyed the battle droids in his way. The young Jedi then found a [[Unidentified Naboo merchant|prisoner]]. After a brief dialogue, Kenobi freed the man, who gave the Jedi a [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]].<ref name="E1 vg" />

Kenobi destroyed the droids under the archway, prompting the [[Tank/Legends|tank]] to leave its position. He then returned to the Queen and led her past the tank. In the next street, they were ambushed by droids, three of which were up on a balcony. Kenobi then met an [[Unidentified R5 unit (Theed)|astromech droid]], but told it he didn't need a [[Astromech droid/Legends|droid]] following him, and the droid remained. Moving along, the Queen and her Jedi protector dueled more battle droids on the way to the hangar. Kenobi then went into the apartment of [[Unidentified Theed woman 2|another woman]] by accident. The woman told him that the gate was locked. Kenobi then leapt onto the balcony, then crossed over the street on an overhanging vine, and opened the gate. During the battle, Kenobi had acquired a blaster, and he used it to destroy three mines on the street to allow the Queen to proceed to the river; he also destroyed more droids. Kenobi then met a [[Unidentified fisherman|fisherman]], and used his boat as a stepping stone to the street. Once there, he Force-pushed a lever to lower the bridge for the Queen to pass over the river. Once across, the two were ambushed by more droids. Further down the street they faced a [[heavy repeating cannon]]. Past that, they joined a firefight with more Palace guards and faced several more groups of battle droids, along with a destroyer droid. The Queen and Kenobi then rejoined Jinn and the others in the Hangar.<ref name="E1 vg" />

{{Endgame}}

====Theed Hangar====
{{Quote|If you are to leave your highness, it must be now.''"<br />"''Then I will plead our case to the Senate.|Qui-Gon Jinn and Sabé, the queen's decoy|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
[[File:Theed_Hangar_side_door.png|thumb|right|300px|The queen's entourage plans their course in Theed Hangar.]]
The group entered Theed Hangar through an unguarded service door and encountered no droids in the hallways.<ref name="TPM junior" /> They stopped to peer in to the main hangar, which was occupied by at least fifty battle droids,<ref name="Episode I Journal" /> who had rounded up the [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] there.<ref name="Episode I" /> Panaka directed the group to a side door and nudged it open to point out the queen's transport, the [[J-type 327 Nubian royal starship/Legends|J-type 327 Nubian royal starship]]. The captain feared that there were too many droids in the hangar, but Jinn insisted that they would not be an obstacle.<ref name="TPM novel" /> Jinn then implored the queen (Sabé in disguise) to come to the galactic capital [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] with him, as he sensed that her life was in danger,<ref name="Episode I" /> contrary to Padmé's expectations that the Jedi would leave for Coruscant alone.<ref name="Episode I Journal" /> Bibble and Panaka protested, claiming that the Trade Federation would keep the queen alive so that she could sign the treaty of surrender.<ref name="Episode I" />

When Jinn insisted again, Bibble changed his mind and agreed that Amidala would need to support Palpatine in the Senate to help free Naboo.<ref name="Episode I" /> The governor assured the queen that he would remain on Naboo to help retain order<ref name="TPM novel" /> and to advocate for the Naboo people.<ref name="Sio Bibble databank">{{DB|character|siobibble|Bibble, Sio}}</ref> Sabé looked to the real Padmé Amidala,<ref name="Episode I" /> who communicated in a coded phrase that she approved of the plan. Amidala used [[Eye/Legends|eye]] signals to communicate with Sabé, and together they decided that the handmaidens Eirtaé and Rabé would come with them.<ref name="Episode I Journal" /> Saché and Yané cried in response, leading Sabé to reassure them<ref name="TPM novel" /> as they reluctantly stayed behind.<ref name="Expanded" /> Panaka selected two of his four Palace Guards to remain with the handmaidens and Bibble.<ref name="TPM novel" /> As the group entered the Hangar bay, Panaka confirmed that they would need to free<ref name="Episode I" /> the twenty<ref name="Mighty Chronicles" /> captive pilots to escape, which Kenobi decided to handle. The Padawan diverged from the main group towards the pilots.<ref name="Episode I" /> 

[[File:Bisected-Droids.png|thumb|left|300px|Qui-Gon Jinn cuts down battle droids in Theed Hangar.]]
The group boldly approached the battle droids, with Jinn causing confusion<ref name="Episode I Journal" /> by ignoring the droids that moved to intercept them.<ref name="TPM novel" /> Jinn approached an OOM command battle droid, [[2163/Legends|2163]], and blatantly stated his intention to take the group to Coruscant. When the droid ordered their arrest, Jinn destroyed 2163 and the other droids with his lightsaber,<ref name="Episode I" /> including [[3B3-1204]], who had been preparing to upload anti-Jedi tactics to the rest of his unit.<ref name="CCG: Theed Palace Limited">{{CCG|set=Theed Palace Limited|cardname=3B3-1204}}</ref> Meanwhile, Kenobi attacked the six droids guarding the Naboo pilots<ref name="Mighty Chronicles" /> with ferocious determination<ref name="TPM novel" /> and ordered the pilots to run. As more battle droids entered the bay and began firing in all directions,<ref name="Episode I" /> Panaka and his guards formed a protective circle around the queen and the handmaidens as they boarded the Royal Starship.<ref name="TPM novel" />

Jinn continued deflecting the droids blaster fire,<ref name="Episode I" /> drawing upon the Force to make accurate parries.<ref name="Mighty Chronicles" /> He observed Kenobi as he ran to the ship with a group of Naboo behind him. Several explosions occurred throughout the hangar and a few Naboo were killed by the battle droid's blaster fire. The Jedi Master ordered his Padawan to get the ship into the air as Kenobi boarded. Not long after, Jinn retreated to the boarding ramp, which closed behind him.<ref name="TPM novel" /> The pilots who had made it to the ship, including<ref name="Episode I" /> chief pilot<ref name="Complete Cross-Sections" /> [[Ric Olié/Legends|Ric Olié]],<ref name="Episode I" /> had activated its [[Headon-5 sublight engine|engines]] by the time Jinn reached the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]]. Alarms sounded and more droids entered the hangar, and Amidala witnessed Bibble's capture as the ship left the hangar.<ref name="Episode I Journal" />

====Astromech rescue====
{{Quote|The power's back! That little droid did it. He bypassed the main power drive.|Ric Olié|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
Olié piloted the exceptionally fast and agile ship<ref name="Complete Cross-Sections" /> out of the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]<ref name="Episode I" /> in [[Standard second|seconds]]. The pilot introduced himself to the Jedi and thanked them for the rescue, and Jinn ordered him to focus on getting past the blockade first.<ref name="TPM novel" /> Kenobi took Binks out of the cockpit<ref name="TPM novel" /> to the ship's astromech droid storage and to keep out of trouble. In [[Realspace/Legends|space]] the starship faced the Trade Federation blockade, where one of the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|blockade battleships]] started firing at the Royal Starship.<ref name="Episode I" />

[[File:R2_repair.png|thumb|right|300px|R2-D2 was the only astromech droid to survive to repair the Royal Starship.]]
When Kenobi returned to the cockpit, blaster-fire knocked the ship from its trajectory and Olié tried to steer it back to its intended path. Jinn tried to find a solution, asking if the ship had a [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking device]], to which Panaka angrily responded that they were not on a warcraft and had no weapons.<ref name="TPM novel" /> The starship was hit directly by blaster-fire, damaging its [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|deflector shield generator]].<ref name="Episode I" /> Olié pressed a button to send out<ref name="TPM novel" /> the ship's complement of six astromech droids to repair the damage,<ref name="Expanded" /> startling Binks.<ref name="TPM novel" /> The droids emerged and entered the airlock as the ship began to level out<ref name="TPM novel" /> as the rest of the crew watched anxiously<ref name="Expanded" /> from a viewscreen.<ref name="TPM novel" />

Olié kept the Royal Starship close to the ''Lucrehulk''-class battleship, meaning that its larger guns were unable to target the ship. The Trade Federation then dispatched a squad of Vulture droids to take on the starship. Within seconds of departing, they were on top of the ship and Olié struggled to speed up and find cover.<ref name="TPM novel" /> Of the droids on the ship, [[R2-M5/Legends|R2-M5]] and [[R2-N3/Legends|R2-N3]] were blasted from the ship's hull while fixing an imbalance in the starboard [[Engine/Legends|engines]], and three more: [[R2-B1/Legends|R2-B1]], [[R2-R9/Legends|R2-R9]], and [[G8-R3/Legends|G8-R3]], were directly hit by Trade Federation fire. The sixth droid,<ref name="Expanded" /> [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], continued on,<ref name="Episode I" /> steadily reconnecting wires while the Vulture droids fired. After one blast of droid fire, Kenobi feared that R2-D2 had been destroyed, but after the sparks disappeared he saw that the droid was still active.<ref name="TPM junior" /> After bypassing the main power drive, the shields were restored,<ref name="Episode I" /> and R2-D2 emitted a whistle of satisfaction.<ref name="Mighty Chronicles" /> Olié commented on the droid's success was able to press down on the thrusters.<ref name="TPM novel" /> The shields held up against several [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]] of intense fire until the Royal Starship was out of the battleship's range<ref name="TPM junior" /> and the droid starfighters fell behind.<ref name="Mighty Chronicles" />

==Aftermath==
===The queen's journey===
====Space odyssey====
{{Quote|And Queen Amidala, has she signed the treaty?''"<br />"''She has disappeared, my lord. One Naboo cruiser got past the blockade.''"<br />[snarls] "''I want that treaty signed.''"<br />"''My lord, it's impossible to locate the ship, it's out of our range.''"<br />"''Not for a Sith. This is my apprentice, Darth Maul. He will find your lost ship.|Darth Sidious and Nute Gunray|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
The Royal Starship's [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] was leaking, meaning that the Jedi were unable to take the queen to Coruscant immediately. Kenobi identified the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] as a suitable destination, as it was poor and out of the way. Panaka rejected the suggestion, as the planet was controlled by gangsters of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Species/Legends|species]], but Jinn reasoned that any of their options would be similar to hiding on a Trade Federation planet, except that the Hutts would not be looking for the queen. Olié, on Jinn's instructions, set their course for Tatooine.<ref name="Episode I" /> 

[[File:Sith_Lords_Trade_Federation.png|thumb|left|300px|Nute Gunray and Rune Haako report the queen's escape to Darth Sidious.]]
Gunray and Haako returned to the ''Saak'ak'', where Sidious demanded a report of the invasion via hologram.<ref name="TPM novel" /> The Sith Lord ordered them to slowly and quietly execute Naboo's remaining government officials.<ref name="TPM junior" /> Gunray informed him that they controlled the northern and western portions of the Naboo's territory, and apprehensively admitted that they had lost Queen Amidala and could not trace her ship<ref name="TPM novel" /> and it was out of their range. Sidious then introduced his apprentice, [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], and told the Neimoidians that the [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] would be capable of finding the queen. After the transmission ended, Haako expressed regret for the situation they had gotten in to.<ref name="Episode I" /> Maul helped send out a countfeint transmission from Bibble, which were transmitted to the Royal Starship.<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

Aboard the Royal Naboo Starship, R2-D2 was brought before the decoy queen and thanked for his actions before she ordered Amidala to clean the droid's<ref name="Episode I" /> carbon scoring<ref name="Chronicles: The Prequels">''[[Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels]]''</ref> in order to maintain the deception.<ref name="Episode I Journal" /> The droid was happy to receive recognition and to be cleaned up.<ref name="Droid to the Rescue">''[[Droid to the Rescue]]''</ref> The disguised queen took time on the voyage to record the events of the Fall of Theed in her journal. She had been haunted to see her planet fall and the image of tanks in Theed and [[Blood/Legends|blood]] in its fountains. Amidala resolved that she would continue until Naboo was free again.<ref name="Episode I Journal" /> Jinn convinced the queen to continue the diversion to Tatooine for repairs, despite Panaka's disagreement.<ref name="Episode I" /> 

====Tatooine and Coruscant====
{{Quote|The death toll is catastrophic. We must bow to their wishes. You must contact me!|Sio Bibble, in a faked transmission to Amidala created by Darth Maul|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
[[File:NabooRoyalStarshipTatooine.png|thumb|right|300px|The Naboo Royal Starship lands on Tatooine after escaping Theed.]]
On Tatooine, Jinn focused on securing a hyperdrive that would suit the Royal Starship. He was able to locate one at the [[Wald's Parts|shop]] of the junk dealer [[Watto/Legends|Watto]], but the dealer would not accept Jinn's [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|Republic credits]]. The matter was resolved with assistance from [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], a boy [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] by Watto, who agreed to win the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Podracing/Legends|podrace]] and buy the hyperdrive with the prize money. Additionally, the Royal Starship received<ref name="Episode I" /> the forged transmission from Bibble<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> claiming that the death toll on Naboo was catastrophic and that the queen needed to contact him. Kenobi warned them that it was a Trade Federation trick and that replying would reveal their position.<ref name="Episode I" /> Panaka later defied the Jedi's orders and replied to the message, allowing Maul to trace their position.<ref name="The Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

Skywalker won the race and was granted his freedom by Jinn, who had placed a wager with Watto. Just as they were about to leave Tatooine, Maul [[Duel on Tatooine/Legends|attacked]] Jinn, but he and Skywalker were able to board the Royal Starship and escape. The starship travelled to Coruscant, where Queen Amidala hoped to present Naboo's plight to the Senate. She was unable to convince the Senate to aid Naboo or condemn the invasion, leading her to initiate a [[Vote of No Confidence/Legends|Vote of No Confidence]] against Chancellor Valorum at Palpatine's urging. Palpatine was nominated for the position in the election [[Supreme Chancellor election, 32 BBY/Legends|election]] and was excited to inform Amidala, claiming that the Naboo crisis would secure his victory and therefore allow him to help his home planet. Amidala, however, decided that she would return to Naboo rather than wait for the Senate to take action.<ref name="Episode I" />

===Occupied Naboo===
{{Quote|Your queen is lost, your people are starving, and you, Governor, are going to die much sooner than your people, I'm afraid.|Nute Gunray to Sio Bibble|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
[[File:BFN_1_Theed.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Trade Federation forces in Theed.]]
Kael and Sykes immediately [[Skirmishes in the Naboo countryside|engaged]] additional Trade Federation forces in the nearby countryside. They went on to form a [[Naboo Resistance|resistance movement]].<ref name="Star Wars: Battle for Naboo" /> Several officers, [[Palmer (Royal Naboo Security Forces)|Palmer]] among them, were were captured by the Trade Federation, but later rescued.<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia" /> Pars Varqom and five others escaped Theed and set up a resistance cell in the [[Penladen Hills]], acting on training Panaka had given them.<ref name="Warfare cut" /> Teckla Minnau and Nandi were separated in their escape from Theed, and Minnau had to avoid STAP patrols and Trade Federation [[Bomb/Legends|bombs]] for days until she found shelter in a [[Unidentified Naboo village (marsh)|marsh village]] for the rest of the invasion.<ref name="Teckla Databank" /> The brutality of the Droid Army and the damage done to Theed unintentionally inspired many civilians and off-worlders to fight against the occupation.<ref name="Fact File 29" />

As a result of the Trade Federation's successful invasion, the blockade fleet, with the exception of the Droid Control Ship, the ''Vuutun Palaa'', dispersed.<ref name="Episode I" /> Theed's upper-class citizens suffered in the detention camps with little food and poor conditions.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> After the transmission of Bibble was sent out, the governor was brought to Theed Palace's throne room for sentencing by Gunray in response to a strike that he had organized. Several Neimoidians; including Haako, Naboo officials, and battle droids were in attendance. Gunray ordered Bibble to be sent away.<ref name="TPM novel" />

===The Battle of Naboo===
{{Quote|Now, Viceroy, we will discuss a new treaty.|Padmé Amidala, after capturing Nute Gunray|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
Following Amidala's return to Naboo, she formed an alliance with the Gungans, who had been driven from their homes in the [[Siege of Otoh Gunga]]. Together they formed a plan to capture Viceroy Gunray at Theed Palace and [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|liberate]] the planet.<ref name="Episode I" /> Panaka contacted Varqom about the plan, but the Palace Guard was too far away to assist and the captain was also concerned that the return of too many Naboo guards would reveal their plan. Instead, Panaka ordered them to attack the [[Penladen detention camp]], saving the Theed gentry imprisoned there. Varqom was surprised to see them furiously tear apart their battle droid guards.<ref name="Warfare cut" /> The [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] marshalled on the [[Great Grass Plains/Legends|Great Grass Plains]] outside Theed, drawing most of the Droid Army away from the city. Amidala, Jinn, Kenobi, Skywalker, Panaka, Sabé, and R2-D2<ref name="Episode I" /> all snuck into Theed through secret tunnels that ended near Theed Hangar.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> There, several pilots, including Skywalker, took control of the [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighters]] there and flew out to attack the ''Vuutun Paala''.<ref name="Episode I" />

[[File:Battle_Hangar.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Queen Padmé Amidala (center) retook Theed in the Battle of Naboo.]]
The queen's group successfully captured Gunray and Haako, and Skywalker destroyed the ''Vuutun Paala''. Maul intercepted the Jedi in Theed Hangar and killed Jinn, but he was then defeated by Kenobi. Jedi [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] travelled to Naboo for Jinn's [[Funeral of Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|funeral]], where he met with Kenobi.<ref name="Episode I" /> and had him recount the events of the invasion, including their rescue of Amidala during the Fall of Theed.<ref name="Episode I: Obi-Wan Kenobi" /> Following that, the [[Freedom Day]] celebrations were held in the streets of Theed.<ref name="Episode I" /> The damage done to Theed in the invasion was repaired by [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], including a revamp of Theed's Palace Courtyard.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> Varqom would later give an [[Royal Archives of Naboo, Vol. 2453|account]] of the invasion, including the Fall of Theed, that was recorded in the [[Royal Archives of Naboo]].<ref name="Warfare cut" />

==Behind the scenes==
===First appearances===
[[File:Nute_Gunray_Theed.jpg|thumb|right|350px|Concept art by Doug Chiang of Nute Gunray arriving in Theed after its capture.]]
The Fall of Theed was created for the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], written and directed by [[George Lucas]].<ref name="Episode I" /> Some scenes involving the Fall of Theed were set inside Theed Palace, the real world location of which was [[Caserta Palace]] in [[Wikipedia:Italy|Italy]]. Filming there took place over four days beginning on [[July 21]], [[1997]], and only took place at night due to the location's tourist popularity.<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> Scenes set in Theed Hangar were filmed on a practical stage at [[Leavesden Studios]], [[Wikipedia:United Kingdom|United Kingdom]],<ref name="Chronicles: The Prequels" /> where filming lasted from [[June 26]] to [[July 18]], 1997.<ref name="Insider's Guide" />

''The Phantom Menace'' was released theatrically on [[May 19]], [[1999]],<ref name="Year by Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> although clips of Theed's occupation were previously seen in the film's trailer,<ref name="TPM trailer">{{SWArchive|subdomain=www7|url=episode-i/news/trailer|text=Episode I Teaser Trailer is Here!}}</ref> released in theaters on [[November 17]], [[1998]].<ref name="Year by Year" /> The first narrative sources to portray the invasion of Theed were the film's [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]], written by [[Terry Brooks]],<ref name="TPM novel" /> and the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace Illustrated Screenplay|illustrated screenplay]],<ref name="Illustrated screenplay">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace Illustrated Screenplay|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace Illustrated Screenplay'']]</ref> both of which were published on [[April 21]] 1999,<ref name="Year by Year" /><ref name="Amazon illustrated">{{Amazon|url=Star-Wars-Episode-Illustrated-Screenplay/dp/0345431103|text=Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace The Illustrated Screenplay}}</ref> simultaneous with another source<ref name="Who date">{{Amazon|url=Star-Wars-Episode-Whos-Who/dp/0762405198|text=Star Wars Episode I Who's Who: A Pocket Guide To The Characters In The Phantom Menace}}</ref> that mentioned the event: ''[[Star Wars Episode I Who's Who: A Pocket Guide to the Characters of The Phantom Menace]]'' by [[Ryder Windham]].<ref name="Who's Who">''[[Star Wars Episode I Who's Who: A Pocket Guide to the Characters of The Phantom Menace]]''</ref> The first source to identify the battle as the Fall of Theed was the CD-ROM ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide]]'',<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> released on [[June 23]], 1999.<ref name="Insder's Guide date">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/videogames/news/news19990623.html|text=''Star Wars:'' Episode I ''Insider's Guide''}}</ref>

===Cut details===
====Revised rough draft====
{{Quote|Do not resist. We will not harm you. We have only come to help you. We bring you peace.|Scrapped line from the rough draft of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace]]|<ref name="Insider's Guide" />}}
Details about the Fall of Theed changed throughout the development of ''The Phantom Menace''. In Lucas's revised rough draft, Amidala receives word of the Trade Federation's approach and intends to warn the Naboo rulers not to fight. Panaka disagrees, and Amidala insists that they will continue resisting the occupation but cannot do so openly.<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> Amidala's stand-down orders were later mentioned in the [[2001]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds" />

Kenobi and Binks&mdash;without Jinn, who did not factor into the main plot until the other main characters reached Coruscant&mdash;reach Theed before the Droid Army. They encounter a curious crowd before a group of Naboo guards arrive to escort them into Theed Palace, and Kenobi convinces Amidala to leave Theed before the attack. OOM-9 snuck the Trade Federation Droid Army into Theed undetected, and the battle began once Gunray ordered them to begin their full scale attack. The Federation uses speakers on military transports to message the Naboo not to resist, and all Naboo security personnel that fight back are wiped out.<ref name="Insider's Guide" />

The Naboo Royal Starship rests on a secret landing platform beneath a fountain instead of in Theed Hangar, and the ship has armaments such as cannons which are crewed by Naboo guards to protect the astromech droids. The Trade Federation starfighters kill some of the guards when they fire on the ship.<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> Other sources such as the novelization specify that the ship has no weapons.<ref name="TPM novel" /> R2-D2 is shocked by electricity while finishing the repairs to the shield generator, but is undamaged. When he returns inside the ship, he repairs the damaged hyperdrive to the extent that the ship is able to jump to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] to Tatooine. OOM-9 reports to Darth Sidious that five ships of the queen's brigade attempted to break the Trade Federation blockade, only one survived and escaped. Sidious correctly believes that Amidala is on board that ship and sends Darth Maul to search for it.<ref name="Insider's Guide" />

====Second and final drafts====
In the revised second draft, Gunray and Haako do not physically enter Theed during the battle. They communicate via hologram, and Amidala's calls Gunray a "little coward." Additionally, no pilots require rescue by the Jedi, and it specifies that seventeen individuals boarded the Royal Starship, including Jinn and Kenobi, Binks, Amidala, Panaka, two handmaidens, four pilots, and six guards. While escaping, Jinn advises Olié to spin the ship to evade the Trade Federation's [[pulsar tracking]].<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> That moment was not included in the finished film<ref name="Episode I" /> but appeared in the novelization.<ref name="TPM novel" />

In the final version of the screenplay, when Jinn and Kenobi rescue the queen, the battle droid sergeant attempts to run away but is destroyed by Jinn using the Force.<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> This moment was not included in the finished film<ref name="Episode I" /> but was included in the novelization.<ref name="TPM novel" /> On board the Royal Starship, Binks is curious about his surroundings and presses on the head of a red R2 unit, causing it to pop up out of place. Binks closes the droid's head after more screws fly out,<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> which occurs in the novelization.<ref name="TPM novel" />

===Adaptation differences===
{{Quote|Are you Queen Amidala of the Naboo?''"<br />"''Who are you?''"<br />"''Ambassadors from the Supreme Chancellor. We seek an audience with you, Your Highness.|Alternate dialogue between Qui-Gon Jinn and Sabé from ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization|<ref name="TPM novel" />}}
The film novelization<ref name="TPM novel" /> describes the queen and her retinue as surrounded by a dozen battle droids when they are arrested in the throne room, but [[Mighty Chronicles]] [[The Phantom Menace (Mighty Chronicles)|adaptation]], written by [[John Whitman]], states that there were twenty battle droids.<ref name="Mighty Chronicles" />

In the film novelization,<ref name="TPM novel" /> and the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (junior novelization)|junior novelization]] by [[Patricia C. Wrede]]<ref name="TPM junior" /> (published [[May 3]], 1999)<ref name="Junior date">{{Amazon|url=Phantom-Menace-Star-Wars-Episode/dp/0590010891|text=The Phantom Menace (Star Wars Episode I)}}</ref> and the [[Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace 1|first issue]] of the [[Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace (comic series)|comic adaptation]]<ref name="Comic">[[Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace 1|''Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace'' 1]]</ref> ([[May 5]], [[1999]]),<ref name="Comic date">{{DarkHorse|url=Comics/98-042/Star-Wars-Episode-I---The-Phantom-Menace-1-of-4|text=Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace #1 (of 4)}}</ref> the Jedi's rescue of the queen is portrayed differently from the film. Instead of jumping down from a balcony, the Jedi are standing in a street when the queen's group and their droid patrol encounter them. Jinn asks for an audience with the queen, and a droid [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeant]] orders his troops to clear out the interlopers. Four battle droids prepare to fire, but the Jedi cut them dow quickly and destroy the rest,<ref name="TPM novel /><ref name="TPM junior" /> and Jinn uses the Force to destroy the sergeant.<ref name="TPM novel" /> 

The junior novelization specifies that Olié was the only pilot to make it aboard the Royal Starship,<ref name="TPM junior" /> but in the film multiple pilots can be seen boarding the ship.<ref name="Episode I" /> In the novelization, when the starship is in space, Jinn orders Olié to spin the ship to evade Trade Federation fire,<ref name="TPM novel" /> which does not occur in the film.<ref name="Episode I" /> The novelization states that a squad of droid starfighters pursued the ship,<ref name="TPM novel" /> while the junior novelization states that only two ships participated.<ref name="TPM junior" /> The [[March]] [[2000]]<ref name="Droid to the Rescue date">{{CargoBay|url=browse/326/40-10|text=Storybooks}}</ref> picture book ''[[Droid to the Rescue]]'', written by [[Gail Herman]] and illustrated by [[Jesus Redondo]], depicts three starfighters in pursuit of the starship.<ref name="Droid to the Rescue" /> This article follows the novelization's description.

According to the novel, the Royal Starship was equipped with five astromech droids, and only four act to restore the shield generator after one is deactivated by Binks.<ref name="TPM novel" /> However, the film depicts R2-R9 as one of five droids conducting repairs.<ref name="Episode I" /> ''Droid to the Rescue'',<ref name="Droid to the Rescue" /> the Mighty Chronicles adaptation,<ref name="Mighty Chronicles" /> and [[2002]]'s ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]]<ref name="Characters">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> state that there were five astromech droids involved in repairing the ship.<ref name="Droid to the Rescue" /><ref name="Mighty Chronicles" /><ref name="Characters" /> The [[2012]] ''[[Star Wars: The Phantom Menace: The Expanded Visual Dictionary]]'' states that all six droids participated in the repairs.<ref name="Expanded" /> 

===Video game appearances===
This battle also appeared in two missions in the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]. The player assumes the role of Kenobi for both missions. In the first segment, ''Gardens of Theed,'' Kenobi infiltrates the city after an Armored Assault Tank destroys a bridge, blocking his path. He follows the path through the gardens and through the gate to the Royal Palace. Along the way the player interacts with Naboo guards. If the player fails to get the code from the first wounded guard, the game allows the player to follow another guard through the gate. The second segment, ''Escape From Theed'' picks up after they rescue the Queen. She and Kenobi get separated from the others and Kenobi escorts her through the city. During the mission he has the option of talking to several characters to get information and game items, although none of it is required to complete the mission. The game's [[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|Star Wars Episode I: Jedi Power Battles: Prima's Official Strategy Guide]] reveals the required paths.

This battle appeared during two consecutive missions in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles]]'', released in [[2000]]. In the first mission, the player (or players) travel through Theed, with the option of bypassing a number of droids or destroying them all to boost their points. The turret droid is the level's boss, which must be destroyed to clear the level. The second level plays out differently from its appearance in other sources. For instance, the player(s), using the avatars of the Jedi, fight various battle droids, including B1 grapple droids. It is necessary to jump up the walls of the palace on balconies to reach another portion of the level. Then, the Jedi are led through a secret passage, under a large tomb, to the palace throne room by a handmaiden they had rescued in the first level; they rescue Amidala from a four-droid escort and lead her through the palace to the hangar, where they face two [[Plasma battle droid]]s. In the ''Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace'' film, the Jedi rescue Amidala and her retinue out on the streets before returning to the Theed hangar to destroy the battle droids guarding the royal starship. The game's [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|strategy guide]] reveals the alternate paths along with the required paths.

In [[2001]] the video game [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']] was released. The game features this battle during the the third chapter; the player assumes the role of Kenobi and plays the scene over three missions: ''City Under Siege,'' ''Within The Palace,'' and ''A Queen in Peril.'' These missions contradict the movie in that Kenobi meets Captain Panaka in the Royal Palace after the latter was supposed to be captured, and the Queen is escorted by a different group of droids when she is rescued. The first segment was written with to follow the 100% completion path outlined in [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|the game's strategy guide]]. Going up and facing the first group of battle droids was necessary to pick up all the game's "location markers" and is off the critical path. In the third segment, destroying the Armored Assault Tank is optional.

The preceding three games contradict each other and the ''Episode I'' film to some extent. They all feature the Jedi's arrival in Theed up to rescuing the Queen or later. This article includes all three pathways and notes specific contradictions where applicable.

This battle also served as the first mission in the [[2000]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo]]'', entitled ''Escape from Theed.'' The player, as Gavyn Sykes in a Flash speeder, was tasked with rescuing Kael and escaping the city. It was not necessary to destroy every droid in the level, just those attacking Kael. Finding the upgrade fulfills the bonus objective, but is not essential. Its placement during the battle is unclear, but it is before Panaka left the planet, as the opening video features his evacuation order.

In 2001 the game ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' featured this battle and the ones leading up to it. The player, in the role of OOM-9, was tasked with leading a force into Theed and destroying the signal jammer. With that objective complete, reinforcements were granted and the player must move the army to the grounds of the Royal Palace, occupying the area (marked with flags) with at least five military units. When the player has fought through to the Palace, possibly destroying military buildings, Gunray orders the construction of a "Monument," the Neimoidian Throne, granting the player sufficient game rsources to do so. When the construction is complete, the mission ends. [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|The game's strategy guide]], besides walking the player through the mission locales and challenges, recommends the player destroy all Royal Security Force military buildings on the journey through Theed. When the reinforcements arrive, the game recommends sending them north to link up with the first army, instead of going west and running into additional fortresses.

In the [[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga|''Lego Star Wars'' game]], the events and characters of the movie are re-stylized as the mute LEGO characters Amidala and Panaka during the game's mission ''Escape from Naboo;'' if only one player is active the other one is AI-controlled. The players must navigate through the level and use the game's telekinetic "Force power" mechanics and build new forms with LEGO studs. The level includes a number of freeplay areas which are not part of the required path. The mission starts in a courtyard and the players must immediately fight a squad of battle droids. At the end of the courtyard is an area where the grapple-carrying Naboo LEGO figures can use their grapples to move to the upper level. Up above the courtyard, the players must travel along the walkway and then jump through a window after breaking it. After that, the players must grapple up another level and destroy three battle droids. When that area is cleared, they proceed up another level by grappling and fight more droids before moving into another room. After clearing that room, the players shot then jump through another window and onto a walkway filled with battle droids. After that engagement, they follow the walkway to a closed gate, which opens when a target is shot with a blaster There they join Binks, Jinn, and Kenobi, who are fighting a group of droids. They proceed by grappling up to another level, where they drop into a walkway and face more droids. To get through the gate blocking their way, they shoot four targets. Passing through, they step on switches placed on three domes which open the tunnels underneath, and then shoot a cage to reveal the tunnel underneath, which they escape into.
